title: 脳科学
subtitle: Brain Science
educationalGoal: Brain science is an integrated study of biology and other scientific disciplines. Therefore, the objective of this lecture is to apply the various knowledge we have learned to the brain. Specifically, based on the premise that the brain is composed of DNA, RNA, proteins, cells, etc., we will continue to study the mechanisms in the brain  that are fundamental for the brain to function. And we want to emphasize that the brain is the only organ that processes information. We are also considering lectures and exam questions and quizzes from this perspective.
advice:
1: What are the shapes and characteristics of the cells that make up the brain? Start by drawing a neuron
2: Understand that there is a molecular basis (i.e., DNA, proteins, their structure and function) that supports brain function
3: There are cells (neurons, glia, and blood vessels) that make up the brain. Understand the role of these cells.　
4: How memory works: how neurons generate electricity.
5: Diseases of the brain: What happens to neurons, will be the final summary of the lecture.
Brain science is built on a foundation of biology.
In other words, it is important for students to have studied the basics of biology in order to understand this class.
In particular, the class will proceed by reviewing the knowledge of "Neuroscience" in the second year and the knowledge of neurons learned in the second year. In addition, students are required to take the first-year course "Structure and Function of Cells" and the second-year course. In addition, the required first-year course "Structure and Function of Cells" and the second-year elective courses "Molecular Biology" and "Cell Biology" will help you understand this course.
